reason: Amino acids built proteins in the muscle cells, so they should also supply the material for the support proteins.

effect: The supporting cells made fibres around themselves, completing the chapter and showing a contrast with muscle cells keeping pulling proteins inside.
reaction: The contrast made the two paths feel connected rather than just repetitive.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the two kinds of proteins was most worthwhile: the results showed how cells with the same DNA can make materials for different jobs.

leastWorthwhile.text: Starting the supporting-cell path felt a little repetitive after the muscle path, although the different result gave it a purpose.

surprise.text: I was interested that supporting cells release protein to build fibres around themselves, while the muscle cells keep their pulling proteins inside.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the messenger pictures and amino-acid label helped explain the pairings.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter to see how these different cells become larger structures, especially the muscle fibres mentioned in the result.
